rationale:
Split into two import-free leaves; the import-dependent analytic core stays in this node, which becomes a non-leaf parent. The supplied proof has three logically separate parts.
(I) Steps 0–1: the annular identity P(σ) + normalDefect V x (B_ρ∖B_σ) = P(ρ) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0. Its only feasible formal route is SimonGMT's kernel-checked Varifold.StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity (StationaryMonotonicity.lean:131), together with normalizedBallMass, annularMonotonicityDefect, StationaryOn and radialNormalSq. All of these live in seven SimonGMT modules outside the frozen contract's import closure.
(II) Steps 3.1–3.3: continuity of the normal defect at the centre. This is pure measure theory.
(III) Steps 2 and 3.4: existence of the density from monotonicity, and passage to the limit σ ↓ 0. This is pure order topology on [0,∞].

Why (I) cannot be a leaf: the active workflow's leaf gate (/runtime/flows/gmt-claude-ceab09671123/_recursive_lean/leaf_verification.py, check_source_delta) accepts only one contiguous `theorem Submission.<name>` insertion. It forbids `import`, helper declarations and set_option; this is the cause of root.constancy-a1.tangent_graph_measure-a1's "leaf proof must preserve the complete frozen base byte-for-byte" failure. A non-leaf, by contrast, may edit Submission.lean freely (parent_verification.check_parent_git_delta). So (I) cannot be a leaf. Nor can this node stay a leaf: without the import it would have to re-derive the whole radial-cutoff computation (Steps 1.1–1.7) inside a single theorem.

Why (II) and (III) are good children: they are genuine, self-contained and reusable, and need only the contract imports.
- centre_defect_limit (II) holds for every varifold, centre and radius, with no stationarity.
- density_limit (III) is the abstract lemma "additive annular identity plus convergent defects gives a limit at 0⁺ and the ball identity". It is reusable for any such identity.
The two children are independent, so the DAG is acyclic and they can run in parallel.

subproblems.title: The normal defect of the annuli B_ρ∖B_σ converges to that of B_ρ as σ ↓ 0
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (ρ : ℝ), Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ ↦ normalDefect V x (closedBall x ρ \ closedBall x σ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (normalDefect V x (closedBall x ρ)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 (3.1–3.3) of the parent node's supplied proof of Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.4 (printed p. 211). That step uses continuity from below of the defect measure and the vanishing of the integrand at the centre; it is made self-contained here. The passage from a sequence of inner radii to the one-sided limit σ → 0+ is added via monotonicity. This is pure measure theory: no stationarity, first-variation or finiteness hypothesis is used, and the statement holds for every real ρ.

Implementation note: this node is a leaf. Its implementation must be the single declaration Submission.normalDefect_annulus_tendsto_closedBall, using only the frozen contract's imports. A scratch proof of exactly this shape compiled and passed the leaf-delta check. The withDensity route below needs no measurability of the integrand.

Notation. Fix N, n, U, V, x and ρ ∈ ℝ.
- G := Grassmannian N n; p_S := Grassmannian.project S; B_s := closedBall x s for s ∈ ℝ.
- For z = (y,S) ∈ ℝ^N × G, f(z) := ofReal(|(y − x) − p_S(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2}) ∈ [0,∞). By definition, normalDefect V x A = ∫⁻_{A×G} f dV (the lintegral of f over A ×ˢ univ with respect to V.measure) for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N.
- D(σ) := normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) for σ ∈ ℝ, and T := normalDefect V x (B_ρ).
- The sets B_s, B_ρ ∖ B_s and B_ρ ∖ {x}, and their products with G, are measurable, since closed balls and singletons are closed and hence Borel.

1. The integrand vanishes at the centre. If y = x then |y − x|^{n+2} = 0^{n+2} = 0 because n + 2 ≥ 1. So the real quotient is (…)/0 = 0 by the convention a/0 = 0, and f(x,S) = ofReal(0) = 0 for every S ∈ G.

2. Removing the centre does not change the defect. Pointwise on ℝ^N × G, 1_{(B_ρ∖{x})×G}·f = 1_{B_ρ×G}·f.
   - If z = (y,S) with y ≠ x, then z ∈ (B_ρ∖{x})×G ⇔ y ∈ B_ρ ⇔ z ∈ B_ρ×G, so both sides agree.
   - If y = x, the left side is 0 because z ∉ (B_ρ∖{x})×G, and the right side is 0 or f(x,S) = 0 by 1.
   Both sets are measurable, so the lintegral of an indicator equals the set lintegral (lintegral_indicator). Hence normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ {x}) = ∫⁻ 1_{(B_ρ∖{x})×G} f dV = ∫⁻ 1_{B_ρ×G} f dV = T.

3. Monotonicity in σ. If σ ≤ σ' then B_σ ⊆ B_{σ'}, so (B_ρ ∖ B_{σ'}) × G ⊆ (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) × G. The set lintegral is monotone in the set (lintegral_mono_set), so D(σ') ≤ D(σ): D is antitone on ℝ. Likewise (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) × G ⊆ B_ρ × G gives D(σ) ≤ T for every σ.

4. An increasing sequence of annuli. For k ∈ ℕ let σ_k := 1/(k+1) > 0 and s_k := (B_ρ ∖ B_{σ_k}) × G.
   - If k ≤ l then σ_l ≤ σ_k, so B_{σ_l} ⊆ B_{σ_k} and s_k ⊆ s_l. Thus (s_k) is increasing.
   - Its union is (B_ρ ∖ {x}) × G. If z = (y,S) ∈ s_k then y ∈ B_ρ and dist(y,x) > σ_k > 0, so y ≠ x. Conversely, if y ∈ B_ρ and y ≠ x, then dist(y,x) > 0, and by the Archimedean property there is k with 1/(k+1) < dist(y,x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt); then y ∉ B_{σ_k} and z ∈ s_k.

5. Continuity from below. Let ν := V.measure.withDensity f. This is a measure on ℝ^N × G with ν(E) = ∫⁻_E f dV for every measurable E (withDensity_apply, which needs no measurability of f).
   - ν(s_k) = D(σ_k) for every k.
   - By 4 and 2, ν(⋃_k s_k) = ν((B_ρ ∖ {x}) × G) = normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ {x}) = T.
   Measures are continuous along increasing sequences of sets (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), so D(σ_k) = ν(s_k) → ν(⋃_k s_k) = T as k → ∞.

6. From the sequence to σ → 0+. D is antitone on ℝ (step 3) with values in the complete linear order [0,∞], so it has a right limit at 0 equal to L := sup{D(σ) : σ > 0}; that is, D(σ) → L as σ → 0 with σ > 0 (Antitone.tendsto_nhdsGT).
   - By 3, L ≤ T.
   - Each σ_k > 0, so D(σ_k) ≤ L for all k. Letting k → ∞ in 5 gives T ≤ L (le_of_tendsto').
   Hence L = T, that is, normalDefect V x (closedBall x ρ ∖ closedBall x σ) → normalDefect V x (closedBall x ρ) as σ → 0+, along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. As N, n, U, V, x and ρ were arbitrary, the statement holds.
proof_key_steps: The normalDefect integrand f vanishes on {x} × G(N,n), since the denominator is 0^{n+2} = 0 and a/0 = 0. So 1_{(B_ρ∖{x})×G}·f = 1_{B_ρ×G}·f, and normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ {x}) = normalDefect V x (B_ρ) by lintegral_indicator.
D(σ) := normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) is antitone in σ, and D(σ) ≤ normalDefect V x (B_ρ), by monotonicity of set lintegrals.

With σ_k = 1/(k+1), the measurable sets (B_ρ ∖ B_{σ_k}) × G increase to (B_ρ ∖ {x}) × G. Continuity from below of ν = V.measure.withDensity f, where ν(E) = ∫⁻_E f dV for measurable E, gives D(σ_k) → normalDefect V x (B_ρ).
Antitone right limit: D(σ) → sup_{σ>0} D(σ) as σ → 0+ (Antitone.tendsto_nhdsGT). This sup equals normalDefect V x (B_ρ) by the upper bound and the sequence limit.

subproblems.title: Limit at 0⁺ and ball identity from an additive annular identity in [0,∞]
subproblems.statement:
Let P : ℝ → [0,∞], D : ℝ → ℝ → [0,∞] and T : ℝ → [0,∞] be arbitrary functions, and let ρ0 > 0 be real. Assume:
(i) P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) = P(ρ) whenever 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0;
(ii) for every ρ with 0 < ρ < ρ0, D(σ,ρ) → T(ρ) as σ → 0 with σ > 0, along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ, in the order topology of [0,∞].
Then there exists θ ∈ [0,∞] such that P(t) → θ as t → 0 with t > 0, and θ + T(ρ) = P(ρ) for every ρ with 0 < ρ < ρ0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (D : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (T : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (ρ₀ : ℝ), 0 < ρ₀ → (∀ σ ρ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → ρ < ρ₀ → P σ + D σ ρ = P ρ) → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < ρ₀ → Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ ↦ D σ ρ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (T ρ))) → ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, Tendsto P (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ) ∧ ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < ρ₀ → θ + T ρ = P ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2 and 3.4 of the parent node's supplied proof of Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.4 (printed p. 211). Those steps give the existence of Θ^n(μ_V,x) from monotonicity of the normalised ball mass, and pass to the limit σ ↓ 0 in the annular identity. They are stated here abstractly for [0,∞]-valued functions. In the parent they are applied with P = densityRatio n μ_V x, D(σ,ρ) = ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) and T(ρ) = ω_n^{-1}·normalDefect V x (B_ρ). Only the order topologies of ℝ and [0,∞] are used.

Implementation note: this node is a leaf. Its implementation must be the single declaration Submission.annular_identity_limit_at_zero, using only the frozen contract's imports. A scratch proof of this shape compiled and passed the leaf-delta check, using MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right, Filter.Tendsto.add, Ioc_mem_nhdsGT, Filter.Tendsto.congr' and tendsto_nhds_unique.

Fix P, D, T and ρ0 > 0 satisfying hypotheses (i) and (ii), and let I := (0, ρ0), the open interval Ioo 0 ρ0.

1. Monotonicity. Let σ, ρ ∈ I with σ ≤ ρ. Then 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0. Every element of [0,∞] is ≥ 0, so D(σ,ρ) ≥ 0, and by (i) P(σ) ≤ P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) = P(ρ). Hence P is monotone (non-decreasing) on I.

2. The limit at 0+. I is nonempty since ρ0/2 ∈ I (as ρ0 > 0), and P(I) is bounded below by 0. Put θ := inf P(I) ∈ [0,∞]. Then P(t) → θ as t → 0+ (MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right). In the order topology of [0,∞] it suffices to show:
   (a) for every a < θ, P(t) > a for all t in some set of 𝓝[>] 0;
   (b) for every b > θ, P(t) < b for all t in some set of 𝓝[>] 0.
   For (a), take I itself: I ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 because ρ0 > 0, and P(t) ≥ θ > a for t ∈ I.
   For (b), b > θ = inf P(I) gives some s ∈ I with P(s) < b. Every t ∈ (0, s) lies in I with t ≤ s, so P(t) ≤ P(s) < b by 1; and (0, s) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0.

3. Fix ρ with 0 < ρ < ρ0. Addition [0,∞] × [0,∞] → [0,∞] is continuous (ℝ≥0∞ is a topological additive monoid). So by 2 and (ii), P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) → θ + T(ρ) as σ → 0+ (Filter.Tendsto.add).

4. The interval (0, ρ] belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT, as ρ > 0). For σ ∈ (0, ρ] we have 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0, hence P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) = P(ρ) by (i). So σ ↦ P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) coincides eventually along 𝓝[>] 0 with the constant function P(ρ), and therefore tends to P(ρ) as σ → 0+ (tendsto_const_nhds and Filter.Tendsto.congr').

5. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is proper, since each (0, ε) with ε > 0 is nonempty, and [0,∞] is Hausdorff. So a function has at most one limit along this filter (tendsto_nhds_unique). By 3 and 4, θ + T(ρ) = P(ρ).

6. Conclusion. P(t) → θ as t → 0+ (step 2), and θ + T(ρ) = P(ρ) for every 0 < ρ < ρ0 (step 5). This θ witnesses the claim. As P, D, T and ρ0 were arbitrary, the statement holds.
proof_key_steps: Hypothesis (i) and D ≥ 0 give P(σ) ≤ P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) = P(ρ), so P is monotone on (0, ρ0).
P is monotone on (0, ρ0) with ρ0 > 0 and bounded below in [0,∞], so P(t) → θ := inf P((0,ρ0)) as t → 0+ (MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right).
For fixed ρ ∈ (0,ρ0), P(σ) + D(σ,ρ) → θ + T(ρ) as σ → 0+, by hypothesis (ii) and continuity of addition on [0,∞].
On (0, ρ] ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 the same function equals P(ρ). Uniqueness of limits along the proper filter 𝓝[>] 0 in the Hausdorff space [0,∞] gives θ + T(ρ) = P(ρ).
